**Question:** When a stretch of digits contains no valid card number starting at its earliest position but does contain one starting slightly later, should the tool keep scanning and redact that later number? (FR-019)

Concretely, in `99 4111 1111 1111 1111` the full 18-digit sequence fails the checksum, but the final 16 digits are a valid card number.

**Why it matters:** This decides whether a real card number that happens to be preceded by other digits gets redacted or leaks through into a shared log — the worst outcome this tool has. FR-019 says the earliest candidate wins and the longest passing one is chosen, but it does not say what to do when the earliest candidate fails the checksum outright.

**Recommended:** Option A — A missed card number is far more costly than the extra scanning work, and "earliest wins" should only apply among candidates that actually qualify. A rejected candidate is not a redaction, so it should not shadow a valid one further along. Note that this needs no change to FR-018: inside an unbroken digit run, any shorter sub-sequence is still flanked by digits and so stays ineligible — the extra matches this finds are the ones that begin just after a space or hyphen.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Yes — after rejecting a candidate, continue from the next eligible starting position, so the example yields `99 [CARD]`. |
| B | No — if the earliest candidate in a run fails the checksum, leave the whole run unchanged, so the example passes through untouched. |
| C | Yes, and go further by also reconsidering starting positions inside an unbroken digit run, which would relax FR-018's rule that a digit-flanked candidate is never redacted. |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
